The Paper Dolphin

Suddenly one day,
A dolphin did appear,
It was blue and smiley,
And happy to be here.

It could fit into small spaces,
It was practical like that,
It visited many places,
Voila! Now it has a hat.

The smiley blue dolphin 
Could dance and soar,
But there were some things
That made him wonder in awe.

“Can I swim?”
“I’m a dolphin after all.”
Perhaps it was time to visit the shore.

The very next day, the dolphin was at the beach,
First snacks, then play,
The water was nearly in reach.

The smiley dolphin was excited,
It was finally time to swim.
WOW! Salty cold water,
What a wonderful thing.

The dolphin floated for a minute,
There was so much to see,
A girl, a bird,
Then the bottom of the sea.

That very same afternoon, a new dolphin was born,
It was pink and glittery,
Something like a dolphin unicorn.

The new dolphin asked, “Can I swim?”
Absolutely not,
We won’t even try.
This dolphin unicorn can only fly.

The End.

Ari loves this book!!! He loves the humour, the animals, and the dancing parts. The is a hilarious picture book about an invasion of pesky animals from Susie Bower,  the author of School for Nobodies.

Mrs Golightly doesn't like animals. And wouldn't you know it - the whole zoo has moved next door! No matter how hard she tries to shoo them away, she finds animals everywhere: a kangaroo on the loo, a giraffe in her bath, and even ants in her pants. What can she do to get rid of these stinky, bothersome creatures?

fulltitle: The Most Boring Book In The World by Charlie Leahy, a read aloud read along story by Tippy Toes Nook
description:
Author: Charlie Leahy
Illustrator: Darcy Prendergast
Publisher: Hardie Grant Children’s Publishing

We give this book  ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ 

This is… THE MOST BORING BOOK IN THE WORLD! That's why nothing interesting, funny or exciting is allowed in it ... and Ari loves this book! He asks for it to be read over and over again, with gut busting laughter at every read. The Most Boring Book in the World is a funny and clever book that breaks the fourth wall. The narrator, a pair of bespectacled eyes on the page, really really wants the book to have only boring things in it. Like a grey cardigan. Or a potato. But the reader can’t help but put weird and wonderful things on every page, frustrating the narrator till the end. This book is super silly - but very enjoyable to read and read aloud. Read by Mum, and pulled together by Dad, we really hope you enjoy this read aloud favourite story book.
